## Selection examples

- **Find cluster markers, score gene signatures, label cells manually or distinguish marker ranking from condition DE**: [`bio-single-cell-markers-annotation`](bio-single-cell-markers-annotation/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/single-cell-spatial/references/bio-single-cell-markers-annotation/SKILL.md`. The marker skill explicitly covers choosing between Wilcoxon marker ranking and pseudobulk condition DE.
- **Transfer reference cell labels, assess confidence/rejection or triage unexpected clusters**: [`bio-single-cell-cell-annotation`](bio-single-cell-cell-annotation/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/single-cell-spatial/references/bio-single-cell-cell-annotation/SKILL.md`. Includes distinguishing novel types from doublets, low-quality cells and batch artifacts.
- **Compare treated/control expression within a cell type across donors**: [`bio-single-cell-markers-annotation`](bio-single-cell-markers-annotation/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/single-cell-spatial/references/bio-single-cell-markers-annotation/SKILL.md`, [`bio-expression-matrix-metadata-joins`](../../expression-de/references/bio-expression-matrix-metadata-joins/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/expression-de/references/bio-expression-matrix-metadata-joins/SKILL.md`. Follow the chosen DE method after resolving that distinction.
- **10X scATAC or paired RNA+ATAC Multiome: QC, ecosystem choice, peaksets, RNA integration, doublets or pseudobulk accessibility**: [`bio-atac-seq-single-cell-atac`](../../chip-atac-chromatin/references/bio-atac-seq-single-cell-atac/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/chip-atac-chromatin/references/bio-atac-seq-single-cell-atac/SKILL.md`. The scATAC workflow covers Signac, ArchR, SnapATAC2 and Cell Ranger ATAC.
- **QC/normalization or integration of scRNA datasets**: [`bio-single-cell-preprocessing`](bio-single-cell-preprocessing/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/single-cell-spatial/references/bio-single-cell-preprocessing/SKILL.md`, [`bio-single-cell-batch-integration`](bio-single-cell-batch-integration/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/single-cell-spatial/references/bio-single-cell-batch-integration/SKILL.md`, [`scanpy`](scanpy/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/single-cell-spatial/references/scanpy/SKILL.md`, [`scvi-tools`](scvi-tools/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/single-cell-spatial/references/scvi-tools/SKILL.md`. Specialist skills cover preprocessing/integration decisions; Scanpy supports standard scRNA analysis, and scvi-tools supports probabilistic and multimodal models. Select by the current need.

## Methods

### anndata

Method: [`anndata`](anndata/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/single-cell-spatial/references/anndata/SKILL.md`.
Role: toolkit. Source-declared name: `anndata`.

Complete source description: Data structure for annotated matrices in single-cell analysis. Use when working with .h5ad files or integrating with the scverse ecosystem. This is the data format skill—for analysis workflows use scanpy; for probabilistic models use scvi-tools; for population-scale queries use cellxgene-census.

### bio-single-cell-batch-integration

Method: [`bio-single-cell-batch-integration`](bio-single-cell-batch-integration/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/single-cell-spatial/references/bio-single-cell-batch-integration/SKILL.md`.
Role: method. Source-declared name: `bio-single-cell-batch-integration`.

Complete source description: Integrate multiple scRNA-seq samples or batches with Harmony, scVI/scANVI, Seurat (CCA/RPCA), fastMNN, Scanorama, or BBKNN. Resolves which method to use for the dataset size and design, how strongly to correct, when integration is the wrong move (confounded batch/biology), how to score integration with scIB metrics without gaming them, and why corrected expression must not be used for differential expression. Use when integrating batches or datasets, choosing an integration method, diagnosing over-correction, or judging integration quality.

### bio-single-cell-cell-annotation

Method: [`bio-single-cell-cell-annotation`](bio-single-cell-cell-annotation/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/single-cell-spatial/references/bio-single-cell-cell-annotation/SKILL.md`.
Role: method. Source-declared name: `bio-single-cell-cell-annotation`.

Complete source description: Automated reference-based cell type annotation for single-cell RNA-seq using CellTypist, SingleR, Azimuth, scANVI, and scmap to transfer labels from a reference. Use when annotating cell types from a reference atlas or pretrained model, transferring labels onto a query, assessing prediction confidence and rejection, or triaging whether an unexpected cluster is a novel type versus a doublet, low-quality, or batch artifact.

Input/context examples (not prerequisites):
- single-cell RNA-seq
- reference atlas or pretrained model

Search terms: CellTypist, scANVI, Azimuth.

### bio-single-cell-lineage-tracing

Method: [`bio-single-cell-lineage-tracing`](bio-single-cell-lineage-tracing/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/single-cell-spatial/references/bio-single-cell-lineage-tracing/SKILL.md`.
Role: method. Source-declared name: `bio-single-cell-lineage-tracing`.

Complete source description: Reconstructs single-cell lineage trees and clonal relationships from CRISPR/Cas9 scars, static expressed barcodes (LARRY/CellTag), or somatic mtDNA mutations using Cassiopeia, Startle, and CoSpar. Use when building a phylogeny from barcode scars, choosing a tree-reconstruction solver, handling homoplasy and dropout, grouping clones from mtDNA, integrating clone with transcriptomic state, or judging whether a state-based fate call is trustworthy.

Method: [`bio-single-cell-preprocessing`](bio-single-cell-preprocessing/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/single-cell-spatial/references/bio-single-cell-preprocessing/SKILL.md`.
Role: method. Source-declared name: `bio-single-cell-preprocessing`.

### bio-spatial-transcriptomics-image-analysis

Method: [`bio-spatial-transcriptomics-image-analysis`](bio-spatial-transcriptomics-image-analysis/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/single-cell-spatial/references/bio-spatial-transcriptomics-image-analysis/SKILL.md`.
Role: method. Source-declared name: `bio-spatial-transcriptomics-image-analysis`.

Complete source description: Segments cells/nuclei and extracts image features from imaging spatial transcriptomics (Xenium, MERFISH/MERSCOPE, CosMx) and H&E/IF tissue images using Cellpose, StarDist, Baysor, and Squidpy. Use when choosing a segmentation strategy (DAPI nucleus + expansion vs membrane-stain whole-cell vs transcript-aware Baysor/proseg vs segmentation-free SSAM) given the available stain; judging whether transcript spillover is fabricating false co-expression and short-range cell-cell signal; and deciding whether the derived cell-by-gene matrix is trustworthy before downstream typing, DE, or ligand-receptor analysis.

### bio-spatial-transcriptomics-spatial-domains

Method: [`bio-spatial-transcriptomics-spatial-domains`](bio-spatial-transcriptomics-spatial-domains/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/single-cell-spatial/references/bio-spatial-transcriptomics-spatial-domains/SKILL.md`.
Role: method. Source-declared name: `bio-spatial-transcriptomics-spatial-domains`.

Complete source description: Identify spatially coherent tissue domains (regions like cortical layers, tumor vs stroma) in Visium, Visium HD, Xenium, MERFISH, Slide-seq, and Stereo-seq data with Squidpy, BANKSY, BayesSpace, STAGATE, and GraphST. Use when distinguishing a domain (a region with many cell types) from a cell type (one cell's identity) and a niche (local cell-type composition); choosing a domain method by tissue geometry (laminar/continuous vs high-resolution imaging vs non-contiguous); tuning the spatial-weight knob (BANKSY lambda, BayesSpace smoothing, SpaGCN histology weight, GNN graph radius) to avoid over-smoothing into blobs or under-smoothing into salt-and-pepper; choosing the number of domains k as a biological decision with k+-1 sensitivity; and reading the Yuan 2024 benchmark with the DLPFC continuous-laminar caveat.

### bio-spatial-transcriptomics-spatial-neighbors

Method: [`bio-spatial-transcriptomics-spatial-neighbors`](bio-spatial-transcriptomics-spatial-neighbors/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/single-cell-spatial/references/bio-spatial-transcriptomics-spatial-neighbors/SKILL.md`.
Role: method. Source-declared name: `bio-spatial-transcriptomics-spatial-neighbors`.

Complete source description: Build the spatial neighbor graph that every downstream spatial statistic (Moran's I, neighborhood enrichment, co-occurrence, spatial domains) inherits, using Squidpy. Use when choosing the graph type (kNN vs Delaunay vs fixed-radius vs Visium hex grid) and understanding why it silently changes every downstream result; handling variable cell density (kNN fixes neighbor COUNT, fixed-radius fixes physical DISTANCE -- each distorts the other); getting coordinate units right (pixels vs microns; Visium array coords are not distance); pruning Delaunay long edges across tissue gaps; running the graph sensitivity analysis almost nobody runs; and knowing when planar section neighbors misrepresent a 3D tissue.

### scanpy

Method: [`scanpy`](scanpy/SKILL.md); Read path: `skills/single-cell-spatial/references/scanpy/SKILL.md`.
